name: Highland Nature Restoration Fund Community Grants
summary: Capital grants for community groups, charities and other local organisations in the Scottish Highlands for habitat restoration, tree planting, wetlands and invasive species removal. The 2026/27 round is closed.

eligibility.rule: Project is for capital costs only
Committed to the Real Living Wage and Effective Voice (Fair Work First)
INNS removal projects remain sustainable beyond the funding period with a site-management plan
Requests none of the listed ineligible costs, such as admin staff time, site maintenance or statutory works
Owns the land, has landowner consent, or a lease of 10+ years before the project starts

documents: Bank statement showing address and account details
Committee, director or trustee list, including relationships (unless in annual accounts)

status.quote: The 2026-27 Highland Nature Restoration Fund is now closed

opens.quote: which opens for applications on Friday 14 August 2026

applicant_types.quote: Constituted community groups Public sector bodies Charities Co-operatives and community ownership initiatives Development trusts

geography.quote: Community groups, charities, public sector bodies and other eligible organisations across Highland are being encouraged to apply

access.quote: Applications will be assessed on a rolling basis

amount.quote: grants available from £2,000 to £25,000 for capital projects

administered_by.quote: The Nature Restoration Fund is a Scottish Government capital fund that supports projects delivering practical action for nature restoration.

effort.quote: Return the completed form and supporting documents

eligibility.quote: The Nature Restoration Fund is for capital projects only.
All applicants must provide a signed statement to show that their organisation is committed to advancing the 'Real Living Wage' and 'Effective Voice' criteria.
INNS removal projects must be sustainable beyond the funding period and have a plan in place to manage sites thereafter

The following costs are not eligible for funding: staff time to administer or manage the project (this can be accepted as in-kind or match funding contribution) ongoing maintenance of any site activities which are a condition of planning or statutory obligations replacement of existing or new infrastructure where there is no biodiversity enhancement
The applicant must have land ownership or lease agreement or landowner consents before the project starts. Lease agreements must be for at least 10-years.

documents.quote: a recent copy of your bank statement with your organisation's address and account details, and an explanation if the address is not the organisation's main address a copy of your latest annual accounts your Fair Work First policy statement
your constitution or articles and memorandum
a list of your committee members or directors or trustees (unless this is included within your annual accounts) including information on any relationships between those listed.

after_award.quote: Once the project is complete, you will be required to report on the actual outputs achieved.
